body: Given the code is practically identical to RD, should check if this issue also happens here: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/108073
I've checked and the issue isn't present in this PR (see the review screenshot below).
Shouldn't decals be after this so the blending happens in linear space?
The value should also be set to `64` here to match the project setting's default value.

DOH! off course, that improve the issue Calinou mentioned up above I think: I'm not entirely sure if reading from the decal texture does any automatic conversion. I'm assuming it doesn't seeing GL_RGBA8 is used, which would be correct (it needs to leave normal and orm data alone).
The decals seem closer to Forward+ now, but the modulate color on the top-right decal seems off (it's more yellow than orange). Perhaps it also needs a color space conversion.
Probably, I wasn't sure if we automatically convert colors or not.
@Calinou I've changed it so the modulate color is converted to linear as well, can  you test if it now looks like you expect?

Works great now 🙂 Compatibility | Forward+ -|- | Filtering of very low-resolution decals with bilinear filtering still looks noticeably different, but it's not a very common use case. That said, I still can't get changes to the decal filter project setting to work. Mipmaps also don't seem to be working, even when using a filter with mipmaps enabled (or anisotropic, but I don't know if this PR handles it).
I'll have another look at the filtering on Monday. Feels like I missed hooking something up.

Ok, it now switches between nearest and linear filtering. I'm wondering if I should change this to apply a dirty flag so it doesn't set this every time, or whether that is overkill.

I'm not sure about the mipmap, it is creating the mip levels, I can see that in RenderDoc, and I've verified we're setting `SceneShaderGLES3::USE_DECAL_MIPMAPS`. But I just copied the code from the mobile renderer so maybe we're missing something still...

Changing the filter mode works now, but toggling mipmaps or anisotropic still has no visible effect (mipmaps remain grainy at a distance).

I'm testing this on NVIDIA for reference, so even nearest + mipmaps + anisotropic should be a supported combination. This particular filtering combination is only well-supported on NVIDIA GPUs, unless performed in software with a shader.

Do we support anisotropic in OpenGL?

I'll have a look if I can figure out why mipmapping isn't working, it's definitely creating the mipmaps but it might not be selecting things on the correct information..

> Do we support anisotropic in OpenGL?

Yes, OpenGL has almost always supported anisotropic filtering, even in the 1.x or ES 2.0 days. It's exposed in Godot too.

I think it should be able to work with decals too, since having anisotropic-filtered textures but not decals creates a visual mismatch for detailed decals. It's not an issue if you just use decals for blob shadows or VFX, but it can be quite visible if you use decals to add detail to surfaces.
Needs ERR_FAIL_NULL ?
I am a little confused by `p_type` being called this way amd being compared against the max number of decals?
Yes, if you look at the definition of the array (`RID textures[RSE::DECAL_TEXTURE_MAX];`), it's an array of this size, so an entry for each type of texture.
I could only find some reference to anisotropic filtering in our 2D renderer, so I'm not sure how this is supposed to work. This is an area I've not really dived into before..

It requires using `glTexParameterf(target, _GL_TEXTURE_MAX_ANISOTROPY_EXT, anisotropy)`, similarily to

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/77c0879cffe8cb7336fab2b7c18dcad2d9a0176c/drivers/gles3/storage/texture_storage.h#L312-L318

Oh whow... That is not confusing at all. So this is all implemented around the 2D renderer, and then we call it from the 3D renderer with a bunch of mapping code that can potentially be overridden, no wonder I completely missed this :)

Ok let me see what I can do with that.

Shouldn't this be multiplied with the modulate color as well? RD seems to be doing it: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/shaders/forward_clustered/scene_forward_clustered.glsl#L1639-L1643

The entirety of the equation is incorrectly wrapped in `srgb_to_linear`, when it should be just the texture sample.
Is it? the data sampled would be in sRGB, I don't think it triggers a conversion to linear, but I could be wrong...
You misunderstood, I meant only the texture sample should be wrapped in `srgb_to_linear`.
